before_releases.name: MIR 5.0.0
before_releases.body:
First MIR 5 community beta: simpler research generation, upgrade-preservation fixes and new Library settings/support exports. GitHub only; stable qualification continues.

- **Smaller download:** the Factorio 2.1 ZIP is 51.8% smaller than MIR 4.7.3. Packaged Lua drops from 47,755 to 28,105 lines.
- **Research and saves:** keeps existing research, settings and earned bonuses on supported upgrades, including older module and cannon bonuses. Caps limit future research without removing already-earned levels.
- **Compatibility:** restores missing Bob's/Angel's research and fixes science, progression and recipe bindings in supported Bob's/Angel's, Krastorio, Py and ATAN setups.
- **Research Library:** per-player search and filters, translated labels, and internal recovery technologies excluded from ordinary research.
- **Settings sharing on Factorio 2.0/2.1:** export full or compact profiles as a copyable string or text file. Full profiles are recommended for support requests.
- **Diagnostics on Factorio 2.0/2.1:** export a local support report from the Library. Attach Factorio's current log separately for startup or crash problems. Nothing uploads automatically.
- **Choose the matching download:** separate builds cover Factorio 0.13 through 2.1. Check the [minimum versions and supported features](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/blob/v5.0.0/docs/support.md#candidate-editions).
- **Experimental older builds:** Factorio 0.18.47 is experimental, best effort and available only on GitHub. Its qualification scope is package metadata and an in-game load/crash check; the in-game check is unverified. The Factorio 0.6–0.12 builds contain basic finite research only, without mod settings, the Library or save migrations; they remain untested best effort. Unzip the Factorio 0.6–0.8 downloads into the mods folder.
- **Before upgrading:** back up the save and matching mods/settings. Test a copy with settings unchanged, inspect research and bonuses, then save and restart Factorio before adopting it. Read the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/blob/v5.0.0/docs/support.md#first-upgrade) before changing Factorio versions or productivity-provider mods.
- **Already-lost research:** the 4.2.1 incident may require a pre-update backup; installing MIR 5 cannot reconstruct erased history. Follow the [recovery instructions](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/blob/v5.0.0/docs/support.md#recovery-from-the-421-incident).
- **Beta limits:** in-game verification of Library keyboard/focus behavior, saved personal views and export files is unfinished. Performance testing continues for heavy modpacks, large factories, save loading and Library memory; extreme loading delays remain under investigation.
- **Full changes:** see the [changelog](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/blob/v5.0.0/CHANGELOG.md).
- **Bug reports:** include Factorio/MIR versions, the mod list, a full settings profile, the engine log and a reproducible save where possible. See [support](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/blob/v5.0.0/SUPPORT.md).

## Startup snapshot

- One included launch per MIR version/workload on Factorio 2.0.77 and 2.1.23; no reboot or cache clearing. Desktop applications stayed running. Intel Core i5-12600K, 32 GB RAM, Windows 10.
- **Graphical initialization (seconds):** Factorio's normal graphical startup log, including mod, sound and graphics loading. This endpoint does not verify a responsive menu. The initial and final no-MIR launches are shown separately because cache/order effects were substantial.
- Heavy means Space Age plus the selected Bob's/Angel's mod set, including graphics packs. These are single-pass observations with different release features; small differences are inconclusive.

| MIR version | 2.0 Base | 2.0 Space Age | 2.0 heavy | 2.1 Base | 2.1 Space Age | 2.1 heavy |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| No MIR, initial launch | 14.46 | 45.72 | 40.22 | 12.86 | 30.24 | 42.06 |
| No MIR, final reference | 8.99 | 18.44 | 26.96 | 8.52 | 20.54 | 28.68 |
| MIR 1 | 9.17 | 18.44 | 27.24 | — | — | — |
| MIR 2 | 8.98 | 18.76 | 28.17 | 8.47 | 20.47 | 29.01 |
| MIR 3 | 10.31 | 19.92 | 31.35 | 9.06 | 22.09 | 33.00 |
| MIR 4.7.3 | 10.24 | 19.89 | 29.71 | 9.08 | 22.26 | 31.77 |
| MIR 5.0.0 beta | 9.05 | 19.13 | 28.00 | 8.28 | 20.66 | 28.88 |
| MIR 5 minus final no MIR | +0.06 | +0.69 | +1.05 | -0.24 | +0.11 | +0.21 |
| Seconds saved: MIR 4 to MIR 5 | 1.20 | 0.76 | 1.71 | 0.80 | 1.61 | 2.89 |

- The 2.1 heavy column uses retained initialization logs from runs whose menu checks failed. It remains a diagnostic comparison; those failures are not counted as menu passes.
- Signed differences are descriptive: a small negative value does not mean MIR makes Factorio faster than running without it. This snapshot cannot resolve small overheads reliably.
- **Observed main menu (seconds):** the following groups also passed a separate Settings response check. These times include the first observed menu, without adding the subsequent interaction-check delay.

| MIR version | 2.0.77 Base | 2.0.77 heavy Space Age | 2.1.23 Base |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| No MIR, final reference | 9.90 | 27.98 | 9.37 |
| MIR 1 | 10.24 | 28.27 | — |
| MIR 2 | 10.01 | 29.10 | 9.40 |
| MIR 3 | 11.60 | 32.44 | 10.01 |
| MIR 4.7.3 | 11.07 | 30.62 | 10.03 |
| MIR 5.0.0 beta | 10.14 | 28.97 | 9.31 |

- MIR 5 reaches the observed menu about 0.7–1.6 seconds sooner than MIR 4.7.3 in these three snapshots. These results do not establish typical added startup cost or factory UPS; repeated controlled measurements remain pending.

## Download and code size

| MIR release family | Factorio 2.0 ZIP (KiB) | Lua lines / files | Factorio 2.1 ZIP (KiB) | Lua lines / files |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MIR 1 | 93.1 | 1,505 / 10 | — | — |
| MIR 2 | 230.6 | 7,439 / 46 | 231.1 | 7,473 / 46 |
| MIR 3 | 1040.2 | 31,420 / 244 | 1042.7 | 31,638 / 246 |
| MIR 4.7.3 | 1415.5 | 46,493 / 283 | 1429.0 | 47,755 / 287 |
| MIR 5.0.0 beta | 688.1 | 28,105 / 114 | 688.4 | 28,105 / 114 |

- MIR 1 uses 1.2.9 on Factorio 2.0. MIR 2 uses 1.9.2 / 2.2.0; MIR 3 uses 2.5.11 / 3.2.11 for Factorio 2.0 / 2.1 respectively. MIR 1 has no Factorio 2.1 build.
- Lua counts include packaged authored data and comments. Files and lines describe code size and structure; they are not a complexity or performance score. Releases differ in features and supported content.

before_releases.name: MIR 5.0.1
before_releases.body:
- **MIR 5.0.1 beta:** startup compatibility fixes and the restored Research Library layout. GitHub prerelease; not a stable release.
- **Startup fixes:** avoid failures with compatible Ironclad mortar-speed changes, Krastorio 2: Spaced Out patch updates within the reviewed major/minor version lines, and train-braking research already provided by another mod.
- **Research Library:** restore side-by-side research and details at normal widths, a readable narrow layout, size/reset controls, retained window position, localized names and details, and responsive search and filters.
- **Performance:** the startup comparisons in the [MIR 5.0.0 beta notes](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/releases/tag/v5.0.0) describe that release only. No new startup, large-factory, or memory measurements are claimed for 5.0.1.
- **Beta limits:** full in-game Library input, saved-view lifecycle, and export-file checks remain unfinished. Large active-factory performance and retained-memory testing remain open. The exact mod archives and complete player configuration for the reported startup failures were not available for reproduction.
- **Before upgrading:** back up your save and test a copy with the same mods and settings. Follow the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/blob/v5.0.1/docs/support.md#first-upgrade).
- **Downloads:** choose the archive labelled for your Factorio version; each label states its minimum version. Factorio 0.18.47 is experimental, best effort and available only on GitHub. Its qualification scope is package metadata and an in-game load/crash check; the in-game check is unverified.

before_releases.name: MIR 5.0.2
before_releases.body:

- **Saved research:** restore five historically paid manufacturing bonuses for affected Factorio 2.0 saves using Space Is Fake 1.0.60. Retain the published upgrade guidance, including the observed limitation for externally disabled research.
- **Library and settings:** show current and maximum recipe productivity, search recipe IDs, preview diagnostic exports, retain personal choices, restore older accepted imported settings values and English setting help, and correct three Russian research names.
- **Configurations checked:** selected Muria 1.9.5, Discovery Tree 1.0.12 and Science Spread 0.9.2 combinations on Factorio 2.1.23 completed affected research and save/reload checks. This does not establish compatibility with every mod combination or the reporter's entire mod list.
- **Beta limits:** full in-game Library input, saved-view/client lifecycle and actual export-file checks remain unfinished. Discovery Tree's None/reset interaction and its Library display still need visual verification. Whole-product large-factory performance and retained-memory testing remain open; no new general performance claim is made.
- **Before upgrading:** back up your save and test a copy with the same mods and settings. Follow the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/blob/v5.0.2/docs/support.md#first-upgrade).

before_releases.name: MIR 5.0.3
before_releases.body:
- **MIR 5.0.3 beta:** cumulative compatibility and saved-research corrections, including the completed 5.0.2 work. GitHub prerelease; stable qualification remains unfinished.
- **Glass compatibility:** keep Krastorio 2: Spaced Out research loading when Crushing Industry replaces its glass recipe. Preserve earned bonuses on both glass recipes, partial work and the research queue through the checked upgrade.
- **Research ownership and settings:** apply cost and time settings to compatible native productivity research; retain separate MIR research when native progression cannot safely represent those settings. Preserve recipe-specific earned bonuses and unfinished work when ownership changes, including destination-force history during force merges.
- **Space Is Fake:** preserve affected paid manufacturing research and inherited-time settings. Keep the historical science requirements on private recovery research so provider removal does not discard queued work.
- **Other corrections:** retain Secretas's finite worker-robot storage research and continue from level 9 with inherited science and effects; improve Russian research and setting wording, including percentage explanations.
- **Configurations checked:** selected Base upgrades from published 4.7.3 and 5.0.2, and Space Is Fake 1.0.60 saved-research transitions on Factorio 2.0.77/2.1.23. The reduced Krastorio 2: Spaced Out 2.0.19 + Crushing Industry 0.6.9/FDSL 0.5.5 case includes paid-state preservation, real glass research and two cold reloads. Some cases seed earned state or accelerate research; they do not establish ordinary research costs, physical production, every mod combination or the reporter's complete installation.
- **Upgrade limits:** retain the documented limits for externally disabled research. These checks do not qualify arbitrary scripted force overrides. Unknown prior ownership is refused before MIR changes its saved research state; keep your original save.
- **Beta limits:** some external weapon-speed research can overlap dedicated MIR research; this remains under investigation. Full Library input, exports, saved-view/client lifecycle and Discovery Tree's None/reset visual behavior remain unfinished. Historical coverage and whole-product factory performance/retained-memory testing remain open; no general performance improvement is claimed.
- **Before upgrading:** back up your save and test a copy with the same mods and settings. Follow the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/blob/v5.0.3/docs/support.md#first-upgrade).
- **Downloads:** choose the archive labelled for your Factorio version; each label states its minimum version. Factorio 0.18.47 is experimental, best effort and GitHub-only; its in-game load/crash check remains unverified.
- **Early downloads (Factorio 0.6–0.12):** finite Base research with fixed defaults only; no MIR runtime effects, mod settings, Research Library, runtime API or save migrations. These builds remain best effort and untested in-game. Unzip the Factorio 0.6–0.8 downloads into the mods folder.
- **Bug reports:** include Factorio and MIR versions, the complete mod list, settings, the current log and a reproducible save where possible. See [support](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/blob/v5.0.3/SUPPORT.md).

before_releases.name: MIR 5.0.4
before_releases.body:
This beta fixes research ownership conflicts while preserving previously earned bonuses.

- Avoid redundant weapon-speed research when compatible native research covers all its effects.
- Preserve electric and Tesla bonuses separately when native research covers only part of their shared upgrade.
- Avoid duplicate coal-crushing productivity with Galore while retaining earned sulfur bonuses and other sulfur effects.
- Handle research events whose technology is missing or no longer valid.

Use the ZIP matching your Factorio version. The modern packages require Factorio 2.0.77 or 2.1.23 respectively. Back up your save before updating and keep the previous package available.

Focused native checks cover the affected research, ownership changes, earned bonuses, queued work, force merges and save/reload boundaries on those exact modern engines. Different provider costs, prerequisites and science packs can change research work and availability. Provider changes that leave prerequisites unmet remain unqualified; keep the original save and mod selection for those transitions.

This is a GitHub prerelease. Full Library interaction/client acceptance and whole-product performance qualification remain unfinished.

The Factorio 0.18.47 package remains experimental/best effort; its native startup/crash smoke remains unverified. Early 0.6–0.12 packages are best effort and not natively qualified: extract their ZIP into that game's mods folder. They provide a fixed finite research subset without runtime features, settings, Library UI or migrations.

before_releases.name: MIR 5.0.5
before_releases.body:
This beta restores Space-policy research for a supported satellite-launch science source and corrects a German Library label.

- Keep research available on Factorio 2.1 with Space Age when the declared satellite-launch source supplies space science, while retaining its science gate.
- Correct the German Research Library sorting label.

Use the ZIP matching your Factorio version. The modern packages require Factorio 2.0.77 or 2.1.23 respectively. Back up your save before updating and keep the previous package available.

Focused Factorio 2.1.23 Space Age checks preserve earned gear bonuses, unfinished research, queued work and detached progress when updating from 5.0.4. Both the ordinary and controlled satellite-source cases complete another lab level, save and pass two cold reloads. These checks do not qualify physical satellite/science production or an entire modpack.

This is a GitHub prerelease. Full Library interaction/client acceptance, historical reconciliation and whole-product performance qualification remain unfinished. Provider changes with unmet prerequisites remain unqualified; retain the original save and mod selection for those transitions.

The Factorio 0.18.47 package remains experimental/best effort; its native startup/crash smoke remains unverified. Early 0.6–0.12 packages are best effort and not natively qualified: extract their ZIP into that game's mods folder. They provide a fixed finite research subset without runtime features, settings, Library UI or migrations.

before_releases.name: MIR 5.0.6
before_releases.body:
This beta prevents unsafe Bob material research from consuming more science while preserving earned bonuses and unfinished work.

- Keep Bob material research unavailable when a recipe can return its own ingredients. On Factorio 2.1, remove that research from the active queue while retaining its partial progress and earned bonuses; eligible research continues normally.
- Restore conditional Marine coke research for Real Industrial Chemistry without changing its research owner or recipes.
- Preserve zero fluid-box extents when applying the pipeline-extent setting.

Use the ZIP matching your Factorio version. The modern packages require Factorio 2.0.77 or 2.1.23 respectively. Back up your save before updating and keep the previous package available.

Focused Factorio 2.1.23 full-Bob/Space Age checks start with bonuses earned in published 5.0.5, preserve paid and partial research through unavailability, and exercise a controlled recipe return. Eligible research and three new Tin levels complete normally; the configured cap, foreign force state, save and two cold reloads pass. These checks do not qualify physical Tin production, arbitrary provider changes or an entire modpack.

Real Industrial Chemistry runtime/save compatibility remains unverified: the available 0.35.8 archive fails upstream on Factorio 2.1.23 even without MIR, and 0.36.1 has not been natively checked.

This is a GitHub prerelease. Full Library interaction/client acceptance, historical reconciliation and whole-product performance qualification remain unfinished. Provider changes with unmet prerequisites remain unqualified; retain the original save and mod selection for those transitions.

The Factorio 0.18.47 package remains experimental/best effort; its native startup/crash smoke remains unverified. Early 0.6–0.12 packages are best effort and not natively qualified: extract their ZIP into that game's mods folder. They provide a fixed finite research subset without runtime features, settings, Library UI or migrations.

before_releases.name: MIR 5.0.7
before_releases.body:
This beta preserves more earned research when updating older Base saves and fixes an upgrade check when moving from Factorio 2.0 to 2.1.

- Preserve earned low-density structure, plastic, processing-unit and rocket-fuel bonuses from MIR 1.0.0, 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 Base saves.
- Preserve earned module bonuses when module research is disabled on the first updated load from MIR 1.1.0.
- Allow the reviewed MIR 4.7.3 Base upgrade from Factorio 2.0.77 to 2.1.23 without rejecting its known research ownership.
- Simplify player reports, local build instructions and source navigation, and update the API guide.

Use the ZIP matching your Factorio version. The modern packages require Factorio 2.0.77 or 2.1.23 respectively. Back up your save before updating and keep the previous package available.

Focused Base checks start from published MIR 1.0.0, 1.1.0, 1.2.0 and 4.7.3 saves. The affected earned bonuses, partial research and foreign force state survive the tested upgrades; new gear research, effects reset, save and cold reloads are checked on Factorio 2.0.77 and 2.1.23. The MIR 1.1.0 case also checks module research disabled on the first update. These are bounded save-preservation checks, not full historical or modpack qualification. Arbitrary scripted bonus offsets remain unqualified.

before_releases.name: MIR 5.0.8
before_releases.body:
This update restores the MIR 4-style Research Library and fixes finite research-speed compatibility.

- Fixed tabs, labelled filters and clearer Research, Settings and help pages.
- Preserved selection and scrolling; fixed narrow-window resizing.
- Continue research speed from level 8 when another mod supplies finite level 7, preserving earned bonuses and unfinished work.
- Show numeric research caps in native descriptions.
- Restored missing setting names, help and dropdown translations.

[Installation, compatibility and upgrade guidance](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/blob/v5.0.8/docs/support.md).

before_releases.name: MIR 5.0.9
before_releases.body:
Fixes a save-loading crash when research costs use a non-default multiplier.

- Preserve earned bonuses and unfinished research while keeping normal science costs.
- Fix the Library Settings page overflowing its window.
- Restore compact effect labels and their original translations.

[Installation and support](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/blob/v5.0.9/docs/support.md).

before_releases.name: MIR 5.0.10
before_releases.body:
Fixes worker robot cargo research conflicts and Space Is Fake science requirements.

- Preserve other mods' finite cargo research and continue after its final level, including WorkerRobotCargoSizeResearch; retain an existing infinite continuation.
- Keep MIR research free of retired white science with Space Is Fake, including expanded science policies.
- Improve saved bonus-history error details while retaining the previous research-cost multiplier fix.
- Back up your save and matching mods before updating. Changing cargo-research providers on an existing MIR save may be refused when previous ownership cannot be established; restore the previous selection and original save in that case.

[Installation and support](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/blob/v5.0.10/docs/support.md).

before_releases.name: MIR 5.0.11
before_releases.body:
Fixes startup with fractional productivity rewards and adds preparation for worker cargo provider changes.

- Fix valid productivity reward settings causing startup errors on Factorio 2.0 and 2.1, including very small rewards.
- Retain the selected Library research while translated search results reload after changing tabs, and remove obsolete science advice from direct-effect descriptions.
- Improve native bonus validation details and detect disabled Angel water-treatment prerequisites before publishing dependent research.
- Add an administrator/server command to prepare earned worker cargo bonuses and unfinished research before adding a finite cargo provider. Preparation covers the ordinary Base-game and Space Age worker research contract. The tested Factorio 2.1.23 route adds Secretas 1.0.38, retains earned bonuses and unfinished work, and passes save/reload checks.

Before adding a worker cargo provider:

1. Protect the pre-change original save and its matching mods/settings. Load a copy with MIR 5.0.11 and the previous mod selection, then run `/mir-worker-storage-recovery prepare` as an administrator or server.
2. On success, save under a new name and exit immediately. Keep the worker level cap and enable setting unchanged through the provider change and while preserved work remains.
3. Add the intended provider to the prepared copy. Check cargo bonuses, current research and queue order before saving and reloading. Use `/mir-worker-storage-recovery resume <force-name>` to append detached partial work when needed.

An already-clamped save requires the pre-change original. Preparation for overhauls and repeated provider changes remains unqualified.

This is a GitHub beta with stable qualification unfinished. Full Ferrum-profile and Factorio 2.0 worker-recovery qualification remain unfinished.

[Installation, preparation steps and support](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/blob/v5.0.11/docs/support.md).

- MIR 5 reaches the observed menu about 0.7–1.6 seconds sooner than MIR 4.7.3 in these three snapshots. These results do not establish typical added startup cost or factory UPS; repeated controlled measurements remain pending.

after_releases.name: MIR 5.0.1
after_releases.body:
- **MIR 5.0.1 beta:** startup compatibility fixes and the restored Research Library layout. GitHub prerelease; not a stable release.
- **Startup fixes:** avoid failures with compatible Ironclad mortar-speed changes, Krastorio 2: Spaced Out patch updates within the reviewed major/minor version lines, and train-braking research already provided by another mod.
- **Research Library:** restore side-by-side research and details at normal widths, a readable narrow layout, size/reset controls, retained window position, localized names and details, and responsive search and filters.
- **Performance:** the startup comparisons in the [MIR 5.0.0 beta notes](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/releases/tag/v5.0.0) describe that release only. No new startup, large-factory, or memory measurements are claimed for 5.0.1.
- **Beta limits:** full in-game Library input, saved-view lifecycle, and export-file checks remain unfinished. Large active-factory performance and retained-memory testing remain open. The exact mod archives and complete player configuration for the reported startup failures were not available for reproduction.
- **Before upgrading:** back up your save and test a copy with the same mods and settings. Follow the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/blob/v5.0.1/docs/support.md#first-upgrade).
- **Downloads:** choose the archive labelled for your Factorio version; each label states its minimum version. Factorio 0.18.47 is experimental, best effort and available only on GitHub. Its qualification scope is package metadata and an in-game load/crash check; the in-game check is unverified.
- **Early downloads (Factorio 0.6–0.12):** finite Base research with fixed defaults only; no MIR runtime effects, mod settings, Research Library, runtime API or save migrations. These builds remain best effort and untested in-game. Unzip the Factorio 0.6–0.8 downloads into the mods folder.
- **Bug reports:** include Factorio and MIR versions, the complete mod list, settings, the current log, and a reproducible save where possible. See [support](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/blob/v5.0.1/SUPPORT.md).

after_releases.name: MIR 5.0.3
after_releases.body:

Preserve recipe-specific earned bonuses and unfinished work when ownership changes, including destination-force history during force merges.
- **Space Is Fake:** preserve affected paid manufacturing research and inherited-time settings. Keep the historical science requirements on private recovery research so provider removal does not discard queued work.

Some cases seed earned state or accelerate research; they do not establish ordinary research costs, physical production, every mod combination or the reporter's complete installation.
- **Upgrade limits:** retain the documented limits for externally disabled research. These checks do not qualify arbitrary scripted force overrides. Unknown prior ownership is refused before MIR changes its saved research state; keep your original save.

Full Library input, exports, saved-view/client lifecycle and Discovery Tree's None/reset visual behavior remain unfinished. after_releases.name: MIR 5.0.4
after_releases.body:
This beta fixes research ownership conflicts while preserving previously earned bonuses.

- Avoid redundant weapon-speed research when compatible native research covers all its effects.
- Preserve electric and Tesla bonuses separately when native research covers only part of their shared upgrade.
- Avoid duplicate coal-crushing productivity with Galore while retaining earned sulfur bonuses and other sulfur effects.
- Handle research events whose technology is missing or no longer valid.

Use the ZIP matching your Factorio version. The modern packages require Factorio 2.0.77 or 2.1.23 respectively. Back up your save before updating and keep the previous package available.

Focused native checks cover the affected research, ownership changes, earned bonuses, queued work, force merges and save/reload boundaries on those exact modern engines. Different provider costs, prerequisites and science packs can change research work and availability. Provider changes that leave prerequisites unmet remain unqualified; keep the original save and mod selection for those transitions.

This is a GitHub prerelease. Full Library interaction/client acceptance and whole-product performance qualification remain unfinished.

The Factorio 0.18.47 package remains experimental/best effort; its native startup/crash smoke remains unverified. Early 0.6–0.12 packages are best effort and not natively qualified: extract their ZIP into that game's mods folder. They provide a fixed finite research subset without runtime features, settings, Library UI or migrations.

after_releases.name: MIR 5.0.5

Use the ZIP matching your Factorio version. The modern packages require Factorio 2.0.77 or 2.1.23 respectively. Back up your save before updating and keep the previous package available.

Focused Factorio 2.1.23 Space Age checks preserve earned gear bonuses, unfinished research, queued work and detached progress when updating from 5.0.4. Both the ordinary and controlled satellite-source cases complete another lab level, save and pass two cold reloads. These checks do not qualify physical satellite/science production or an entire modpack.

This is a GitHub prerelease. Full Library interaction/client acceptance, historical reconciliation and whole-product performance qualification remain unfinished. Provider changes with unmet prerequisites remain unqualified; retain the original save and mod selection for those transitions.

The Factorio 0.18.47 package remains experimental/best effort; its native startup/crash smoke remains unverified. Early 0.6–0.12 packages are best effort and not natively qualified: extract their ZIP into that game's mods folder. They provide a fixed finite research subset without runtime features, settings, Library UI or migrations.

after_releases.name: MIR 5.0.6
after_releases.body:
This beta prevents unsafe Bob material research from consuming more science while preserving earned bonuses and unfinished work.

- Keep Bob material research unavailable when a recipe can return its own ingredients. On Factorio 2.1, remove that research from the active queue while retaining its partial progress and earned bonuses; eligible research continues normally.
- Restore conditional Marine coke research for Real Industrial Chemistry without changing its research owner or recipes.
- Preserve zero fluid-box extents when applying the pipeline-extent setting.

Use the ZIP matching your Factorio version. The modern packages require Factorio 2.0.77 or 2.1.23 respectively. Back up your save before updating and keep the previous package available.

Focused Factorio 2.1.23 full-Bob/Space Age checks start with bonuses earned in published 5.0.5, preserve paid and partial research through unavailability, and exercise a controlled recipe return. Eligible research and three new Tin levels complete normally; the configured cap, foreign force state, save and two cold reloads pass. These checks do not qualify physical Tin production, arbitrary provider changes or an entire modpack.

Real Industrial Chemistry runtime/save compatibility remains unverified: the available 0.35.8 archive fails upstream on Factorio 2.1.23 even without MIR, and 0.36.1 has not been natively checked.

This is a GitHub prerelease. Full Library interaction/client acceptance, historical reconciliation and whole-product performance qualification remain unfinished. Provider changes with unmet prerequisites remain unqualified; retain the original save and mod selection for those transitions.

The Factorio 0.18.47 package remains experimental/best effort; its native startup/crash smoke remains unverified. Early 0.6–0.12 packages are best effort and not natively qualified: extract their ZIP into that game's mods folder. They provide a fixed finite research subset without runtime features, settings, Library UI or migrations.

after_releases.name: MIR 5.0.7
after_releases.body:
This beta preserves more earned research when updating older Base saves and fixes an upgrade check when moving from Factorio 2.0 to 2.1.

- Preserve earned low-density structure, plastic, processing-unit and rocket-fuel bonuses from MIR 1.0.0, 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 Base saves.
- Preserve earned module bonuses when module research is disabled on the first updated load from MIR 1.1.0.
- Allow the reviewed MIR 4.7.3 Base upgrade from Factorio 2.0.77 to 2.1.23 without rejecting its known research ownership.
- Simplify player reports, local build instructions and source navigation, and update the API guide.

Use the ZIP matching your Factorio version. The modern packages require Factorio 2.0.77 or 2.1.23 respectively. Back up your save before updating and keep the previous package available.

Focused Base checks start from published MIR 1.0.0, 1.1.0, 1.2.0 and 4.7.3 saves. The affected earned bonuses, partial research and foreign force state survive the tested upgrades; new gear research, effects reset, save and cold reloads are checked on Factorio 2.0.77 and 2.1.23. The MIR 1.1.0 case also checks module research disabled on the first update. These are bounded save-preservation checks, not full historical or modpack qualification. Arbitrary scripted bonus offsets remain unqualified.

after_releases.name: MIR 5.0.8
after_releases.body:
This update restores the MIR 4-style Research Library and fixes finite research-speed compatibility.

- Fixed tabs, labelled filters and clearer Research, Settings and help pages.
- Preserved selection and scrolling; fixed narrow-window resizing.
- Continue research speed from level 8 when another mod supplies finite level 7, preserving earned bonuses and unfinished work.
- Show numeric research caps in native descriptions.
- Restored missing setting names, help and dropdown translations.

[Installation, compatibility and upgrade guidance](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/blob/v5.0.8/docs/support.md).

after_releases.name: MIR 5.0.9

after_releases.name: MIR 5.0.10
after_releases.body:
Fixes worker robot cargo research conflicts and Space Is Fake science requirements.

- Preserve other mods' finite cargo research and continue after its final level, including WorkerRobotCargoSizeResearch; retain an existing infinite continuation.
- Keep MIR research free of retired white science with Space Is Fake, including expanded science policies.
- Improve saved bonus-history error details while retaining the previous research-cost multiplier fix.
- Back up your save and matching mods before updating. Changing cargo-research providers on an existing MIR save may be refused when previous ownership cannot be established; restore the previous selection and original save in that case.

[Installation and support](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/blob/v5.0.10/docs/support.md).

after_releases.name: MIR 5.0.11
after_releases.body:
Fixes startup with fractional productivity rewards and adds preparation for worker cargo provider changes.

- Fix valid productivity reward settings causing startup errors on Factorio 2.0 and 2.1, including very small rewards.
- Retain the selected Library research while translated search results reload after changing tabs, and remove obsolete science advice from direct-effect descriptions.
- Improve native bonus validation details and detect disabled Angel water-treatment prerequisites before publishing dependent research.
- Add an administrator/server command to prepare earned worker cargo bonuses and unfinished research before adding a finite cargo provider. Preparation covers the ordinary Base-game and Space Age worker research contract. The tested Factorio 2.1.23 route adds Secretas 1.0.38, retains earned bonuses and unfinished work, and passes save/reload checks.

Before adding a worker cargo provider:

1. Protect the pre-change original save and its matching mods/settings. Load a copy with MIR 5.0.11 and the previous mod selection, then run `/mir-worker-storage-recovery prepare` as an administrator or server.
2. On success, save under a new name and exit immediately. Keep the worker level cap and enable setting unchanged through the provider change and while preserved work remains.
3. Add the intended provider to the prepared copy. Check cargo bonuses, current research and queue order before saving and reloading. Use `/mir-worker-storage-recovery resume <force-name>` to append detached partial work when needed.

An already-clamped save requires the pre-change original. Preparation for overhauls and repeated provider changes remains unqualified.

This is a GitHub beta with stable qualification unfinished. Full Ferrum-profile and Factorio 2.0 worker-recovery qualification remain unfinished.

[Installation, preparation steps and support](https://github.com/Julesc013/more-infinite-research/blob/v5.0.11/docs/support.md).
